source: IMF Country Report No. 23/225 (Dominican Republic, 2023 Article IV): Table 2b, central government subsidies, electricity, RD$80 bn in 2022 (actual; PDF p.37); Table 1, 2022 average rate 55.0 RD$/US$ (PDF p.35). The same RD$80 bn is in IMF Country Report No. 24/294 (PDF p.35)
basis: Beta v4 P4: the 2022 central-government current subsidy to the public electricity companies (CDEEE and the EDEs), covering losses and the tariff gap (tariffs frozen from July 2022). DOM is not in the IEA 2022 electricity subsidy data, so GTAP 12 §12.4.3 p.29's condition holds. The IMF figure replaces the DIGEPRES figure reported by elDinero (RD$99.3 bn, US$1,802.7 m), which appears to include capital transfers; that is kept as an upper bound. The booked amount is at most the 90 percent rule's shortfall (S11-Relysub).
